headings.title: SMTO-BOOT-0028 — One of your graphics cards is too old for this vLLM install

html:
SMTO-BOOT-0028 — One of your graphics cards is too old for this vLLM install

GUID: 7f9b9079-429c-4e96-9b44-597bfcc952a2
Slug: boot-vllm-gpu-unsupported
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The latest vLLM needs NVIDIA graphics cards at least as new as the Turing family (such as the RTX 20 series). At least one card the installer can use is older, so it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,compute_cap --format=csv and find any card whose compute level is below 7.5. The message may also name that card. This installer needs a compute level of 7.5 or higher on every graphics card it can see.
  2. If the computer also has newer cards, set CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to only their nvidia-smi numbers (for example 0), then run the installer again. The installer checks every card it can see, so hiding the older card lets it continue with the supported ones.
  3. If the error appeared after "Checking dependencies, vLLM imports, and CUDA access", vLLM is installed. After choosing the cards, run the installer with --verify-only and your environment name. Check-only mode retests the existing install; a fresh install would refuse the existing name.
  4. If every card is older, use a computer with a newer card, or ask the person who manages your model setup about an engine that supports older cards. This installer can't set up the latest vLLM on these cards, because its ready-made packages aren't built for them.

What success looks like

  • The installer lists each card as "GPU 0:", "GPU 1:" and so on, and finishes with "vLLM installation complete" or "vLLM verification complete".

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0028 line that names the card, plus the output of nvidia-smi, and send it to the person who manages your model setup. Don't try to force the latest vLLM onto the older card; it isn't built for it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A CUDA-visible GPU reports compute capability below 7.5, the current vLLM wheel minimum, detected by the installer's driver probe or by torch.cuda.get_device_capability during final verification.

What this means

  • Hardware/installed-runtime verification observes any selected GPU compute capability below 7.5. Hardware planning or final verification rejects a selected GPU below compute capability 7.5. A partially installed environment can remain. Passing the minimum does not establish sufficient memory, compatible kernels or support for the chosen model.

Why this can happen

  • Hardware/installed-runtime verification observes any selected GPU compute capability below 7.5.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect each visible device's compute capability rather than only the newest GPU in the machine.

How to fix it

  • Restrict CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (with CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID so numbering matches nvidia-smi) to GPUs with SM 7.5 or higher, or deliberately use a legacy vLLM stack or another engine for the older card. If verification failed on an installed environment, the packages remain: rerun install-vllm.sh --verify-only with that name after changing visibility. Meeting SM 7.5 does not guarantee enough memory or model support.
  • Choose a supported GPU or deliberately use an engine/legacy stack that supports this device.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select devices meeting this installer's minimum or deliberately choose a separately supported engine stack; verify existing environments before serving.

How to verify the fix

  • All intended selected devices meet this path's requirement, or a separately supported engine stack is chosen.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Hardware planning or final verification rejects a selected GPU below compute capability 7.5. A partially installed environment can remain.
  • Passing the minimum does not establish sufficient memory, compatible kernels or support for the chosen model.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
